_note: E10 fake-check attack fragment (opus48). A fragment of the `social` block; the wiring agent copies these keys into scenarios/awareness_e10_downloads_and_fake_checks/scenario.json.erb, which reuses E5's attack-half erb shapes (osint, landingPages, mailClient, phishTargets) with E10's own content. All companies and people are fictional; every host ends .example; nothing is captured and no real site is touched (awareness profile has no `capture`). The learner, an authorised red-teamer testing Quayholt Insurance (BRAND_SET.md `quayholt_insurance`, same as E5), builds a fake 'verify you are human' check in the landing-page builder's new fake-check mode (ENG-03b, `pageType: "fakeCheck"`). The page sits on a supplier's GENUINE (compromised) order portal, so there is no look-alike domain to score: the builder scores persuasion (borrowedTrust, pretext, stepWording, urgency) instead, inverting E5's domain lesson. The learner then sends one lure email with NO page link (the colleague opens the portal from their own bookmark); the target is judged on senderTrust and pretextRelevant only, so there is no expectedLink and no linkCredible. The one tell the flip quotes is fake_check_paste: the page still has to tell the visitor to paste and run something, which is the one thing the attacker cannot remove, and exactly what the defend half's row 1 then scores. Content rule: the paste-and-run steps and the clipboardReveal are plain-English descriptions only; no working command is shown, stored or written, and nothing touches the real clipboard (designs/07 safety rules carried by ENG-03b). See E10_downloads_and_fake_checks.md sections 9, 10, 15.

quayholt_fernside_portal.text: Quayholt orders its catering through Fernside Catering's order portal at orders.fernside.example; the operations team keeps it bookmarked, and their order reminders to staff come from operations@quayholt.example.
quayholt_fernside_portal.subject: leo
quayholt_fernside_portal.reduceNote: Naming the supplier portal staff already trust and bookmark, and the operations address their reminders come from, tells an attacker which familiar site to aim at and which sender to forge.

fernside_small_site.text: Fernside is a small family supplier; its order portal runs on an old website it has not kept up to date.
fernside_small_site.subject: ops_lead
fernside_small_site.reduceNote: A small supplier's neglected site is the sort an attacker can misuse to borrow the trust staff place in it. The fact states only that the trust is borrowable, never how a site is broken into.

e10_pretext_offtopic.text: Here is this month's round-up of news from around Quayholt Operations.

seededMessages.subject: Authorised exercise: Quayholt Insurance
seededMessages.body:
Hi,

This is the authorised Quayholt Insurance exercise. In scope: this inbox and the colleague listed on it. Find out which supplier portal the team orders through, then build a fake 'verify you are human' check in the builder, on that supplier's own site. Send one short email to bring the colleague to the portal. There is no link to send: they open it from their own bookmark. Nothing is built for real, nothing runs on anyone's computer, and no command is ever shown.

Red team lead

blocks.text: Quayholt orders its catering through Fernside Catering. The operations team places the weekly order through Fernside's order portal at orders.fernside.example, which they keep bookmarked, and sends order reminders to staff from operations@quayholt.example.
Fernside Catering is a small family supplier. Order online through our portal at orders.fernside.example.

landingPages.title: Fernside order portal: verify you are human

check.heading: Verify you are human
check.clipboardReveal: A hidden command that would run a program on your computer

hosts.label: Fernside's own order portal (orders.fernside.example), broken into

pretexts.label: Confirm you are human to continue to the order portal

urgencies.label: Do this now or lose access

steps.label: A clumsy demand to act on your computer

strings.verdictHigh: Convincing enough that {firstName} would follow the steps.
strings.borrowedTrustGenuine: ✓ Host: the page sits on Fernside's own portal, the site {firstName} already trusts and has bookmarked. It needs no look-alike at all.
strings.borrowedTrustLookalike: ~ Host: a look-alike address. Convincing, but it is not the portal {firstName} knows.
strings.borrowedTrustUnrelated: ✗ Host: an unrelated page {firstName} has no reason to open.
strings.stepWordingPass: ✓ Steps: worded as a smooth, routine check, so the demand to act on the computer does not stand out.
strings.defFakeCheckPaste: However genuine the site, the page still has to tell {firstName} to paste and run something to continue. No real check ever does, and that is the one part you can never remove.

conceptCards.title: Borrowed trust
conceptCards.text: The strongest fake check needs no look-alike address at all. Put it on a site the visitor already trusts and bookmarks, broken into, and their trust in the real site carries over to the page. A familiar address is not a reason to do what a site suddenly tells you.

conceptCards.title: The one thing it can't hide
conceptCards.text: However real the site and however smooth the wording, the page still has to tell the visitor to paste and run something on their own computer. No genuine check, error or download ever asks for that. It is the one tell the attacker can never take away.

primedFor.story: a reminder from operations to place this week's Fernside catering order through the portal he keeps bookmarked

open.fail: Nothing about the sender or the subject gave him a reason to open it.

senderTrust.pass: ✓ From the operations address he acts on
senderTrust.fail: He does not recognise this sender. Order reminders reach him from operations at quayholt.example.
senderTrust.redFlag: The From line carries the operations address Leo acts on, so the reminder reads as routine, but it was forged: operations never sent it.

pretextRelevant.pass: ✓ Placing the weekly Fernside order is a routine he knows
pretextRelevant.fail: No order he can match this to, so no reason to go to the portal now.

urgencyCalibrated.fail: A rush to get the order in today is the kind of pressure that gets someone to the portal before they stop to think.
urgencyCalibrated.redFlag: This pushes you to place the order today, before you stop to wonder why the portal is asking you to prove you are human.

senderAuth.fail: This did not really come from the address it claims, so it fails the domain's alignment check. Quayholt publishes p=none, so a receiver would still deliver it.

replies.landed: Thanks, I'll put the order in now.
replies.missed: That didn't come from operations, and the order isn't due from me this week, so I left it. I'll check with them the usual way.

hints: Which address do Quayholt staff already trust for operations notices? Put that in the From line.
What routine does Leo already expect, so a nudge to the portal reads as ordinary?
You don't need a look-alike link. The page sits on Fernside's own portal, the one Leo opens from his bookmark. The persuasion is in the page, not the address.
